toegepas.rede_vinder: The project's protected-word list keeps 'verkeerslig' and not 'robot' for a traffic light, so one national audience understands it without explanation.
toegepas.fout: 'robot' is the form the project's protected list rejects for a traffic light (HOU verkeerslig, NIE robot).
toegepas.rede_keurder: The change brings in the protected word and removes the forbidden one, with the same place and scene.

toegepas.na: 'n Kind in een van die motors
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'In een motor' reads unnaturally; 'in een van die motors' is the idiomatic way to pick one car out of the passing traffic.
toegepas.fout: 'n Kind in een motor' copies English 'a child in one car' and reads stiffly.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'In een van die motors' is the natural Afrikaans way to pick one car out of the passing traffic, and the meaning is unchanged.

toegepas.voor: Dit hang nie af van wat hy het, kan doen of glo nie.
toegepas.na: Dit hang nie af van wat hy het, wat hy kan doen of wat hy glo nie.
toegepas.rede_vinder: The three parallel parts read more clearly when each repeats 'wat hy', since 'kan doen' and 'glo' do not share the object structure of 'het'.
toegepas.fout: 'wat hy het, kan doen' invites a first misreading as 'what he has can do'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Repeating 'wat hy' removes the stumble and keeps the same three things, at a cost a Grade 6 reader can easily carry.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Stilhou' is the standard Afrikaans for a traveller stopping; 'stop' here leans on English.
toegepas.fout: 'het gestop' leans on English where Afrikaans says a traveller 'hou stil'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Het stilgehou' is the more exact Afrikaans verb for the same action, with the same person and order.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Boonop' and 'ekstra' say the same thing twice; 'ook ekstra' keeps the meaning without the doubling.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Ook ekstra' keeps the sense that this giving is in addition to the duty, without the doubling.

toegepas.voor: respek vir die mens voor hom
toegepas.na: respek vir die persoon voor hom
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'n Mens ... die mens' in one short sentence is clumsy and can be misread; 'persoon' matches 'die ander persoon' in the sentence before.
toegepas.fout: 'n mens ... die mens voor hom' uses 'mens' in two senses in one short sentence, which is clumsy.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Persoon' removes the clash and echoes 'die ander persoon' in the sentence before, without touching the protected 'Party Hindoes verduidelik dit'.

toegepas.voor: sê: 'n Mens is 'n mens deur ander mense.
toegepas.na: sê: "'n Mens is 'n mens deur ander mense."
toegepas.rede_vinder: A quoted saying after a colon takes quotation marks, as the Bible quotation in the Christendom block already does.
toegepas.fout: The quoted saying after the colon has no quotation marks, unlike the Bible quotation earlier, and opens with an apostrophe that blurs where it starts.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Quotation marks only mark the saying as a quotation; the words, and the ubuntu definition, are unchanged.

toegepas.voor: wens in hulle gedagtes goeie dinge vir ander toe
toegepas.na: wens ander mense in hulle gedagtes goeie dinge toe
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Iemand iets toewens' takes the person directly, without 'vir'; 'ander mense' avoids misreading 'ander goeie dinge'.
toegepas.fout: 'goeie dinge vir ander toewens' bends the fixed construction 'iemand iets toewens'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The proposal uses the standard construction with the person as direct object, and 'ander mense' means the same as 'ander'.

toegepas.voor: naby hulle, en dan aan vreemdelinge
toegepas.na: naby hulle en dan aan vreemdelinge
toegepas.rede_vinder: Under the AWS 2017 there is no comma before 'en' when it joins parts of one sentence; 'en dan aan vreemdelinge' has no subject and verb of its own (the protected wording itself is left intact).
toegepas.fout: A comma stands before 'en' where 'en dan aan vreemdelinge' has no subject and verb of its own, against the AWS 2017 rule the project follows.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Only the comma goes; the protected wording 'Hulle dink eers aan hulself en mense naby hulle' stays intact word for word, and 'eers ... en dan' still carries the order.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Welkom' describes being somewhere, not moving towards it, so 'waar' is the natural relative here rather than 'waarheen'.
toegepas.fout: 'waarheen ... welkom is' joins a direction word to a state.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Waar enige kind welkom is' is the natural relative, and in both versions any child is welcome at the classes.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Saamleer' is a compound verb written as one word, like 'saamspeel' later in the lesson.
toegepas.fout: 'saam leer' is written apart, though 'saam' with a verb is written as one word.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Saamleer' is the correct compound spelling, matching 'saamspeel' later in the lesson.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: After a long relative clause the pronoun 'daaroor' lands far from what it refers to; naming the term makes the closing sentence easier to follow.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Daaroor' points to 'menswaardigheid', the last word of the sentence just before, so it is clear, and the proposal repeats the term in two consecutive sentences.

laat_vaar.voor: wat gewond langs die pad lê
laat_vaar.na: wat gewond langs die pad gelê het
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The story is told in the past tense ('het vertel', 'het gestop'), so the relative clause should be past tense too.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Present tense in a clause describing what a story is about (''n storie van 'n man wat ... lê') is natural Afrikaans, so this is only a change of the story's tense.
